cards.explanation: The answer is enemies. The LORD says, "I have given the beloved of My soul into the hands of her enemies." (Jeremiah 12:7) Notice He calls her the beloved of His soul, and the very next thing is that heavy handing over. I think this is a hard verse to read out loud, so take your time with it, friends.

The answer is that she roared against Him. The LORD says, "She has roared against Me…" (Jeremiah 12:8) A lion in the forest doesn't whisper, and this one is roaring at Him, friends. That's the picture He chose, so we keep it just like that.

The answer is False. The text says the other birds of prey are "…circling against her?" (Jeremiah 12:9) They aren't there to protect the speckled bird, friends. It's a picture of a bird with trouble circling overhead.

The answer is all the beasts of the field. The LORD says, "Go, gather all the beasts of the field; bring them to devour her." (Jeremiah 12:9) All of them, every beast in the field. I'd be nervous just reading that list, friends.

The answer is many shepherds. The LORD says, "Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard; they have trampled My plot of ground." (Jeremiah 12:10) Shepherds are supposed to look after things, so that line stings, friends. Many of them, and the plot got trampled.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "All the land is laid waste, but no man takes it to heart." (Jeremiah 12:11) The land is mourning and nobody takes it to heart. I think that's the sad part, friends, so let it sit a second.

The answer is LORD. The verse says "…the sword of the LORD devours from one end of the earth to the other." (Jeremiah 12:12) It's His sword, friends, and it reaches from one end to the other. Then comes the line, "No flesh has peace."

The answer is the LORD's fierce anger. The verse says, "Bear the shame of your harvest because of the fierce anger of the LORD." (Jeremiah 12:13) It's tied right to the thorns they harvested after sowing wheat. That's the only reason the verse gives, friends, so we stick with it.

The answer is that He will uproot them from their land. The LORD says, "…I am about to uproot them from their land…" (Jeremiah 12:14) These are the evil neighbors who attack the inheritance He bequeathed to His people Israel. Uproot is the word, friends, so remember it.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "…and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them." (Jeremiah 12:14) So it's the neighbors, and Judah is uprooted from among them too. It's a heavy line, friends, and it's right there in the text.

The answer is False. After the uprooting, the LORD says, "…I will once again have compassion on them and return each one to his inheritance and to his land." (Jeremiah 12:15) So the verse says compassion again, friends, not never. That's a good sentence to carry out of the passage.
The answer is land. The LORD says He will "…return each one to his inheritance and to his land." (Jeremiah 12:15) Each one, to his own land, friends. That's a hopeful line after all that uprooting.

The answer is Baal. The LORD says the neighbors once taught His people to swear by Baal, a false god. (Jeremiah 12:16) Now He says they can learn to swear by His name, saying, "As surely as the LORD lives…" The same people who taught the wrong oath are invited to learn the right one, friends.

The answer is that they will be established among His people. The LORD says, "…then they will be established among My people." (Jeremiah 12:16) The neighbors have to learn the ways of His people and swear by His name first, friends. After that comes the welcome.

The answer is obey. The LORD says, "But if they will not obey, then I will uproot that nation; I will uproot it and destroy it, declares the LORD." (Jeremiah 12:17) It's the other side of the if from verse 16, friends. These are the closing words of the message, so they land hard.
